title: Ultraviolet obstructions to gravitational clocks in null-cone quantum gravity
subtitle: In the linearised sector, Weyl, normal and Wick ordering each fail to give the clock that a recent quantum-gravity proposal needs
shortTitle: Why the null-cone gravitational clock is not an operator
oneLine: In the linearised sector of a new null-cone quantisation of gravity, the three natural ways of defining its gravitational clock each fail to give an operator; the Wick-ordered clock has the right vacuum reading but its form is not closable
abstract: A proposal posted on 25 November 2026 by Chandrasekaran quantises gravity on intersecting null cones and uses a gravitational clock, the time light needs to reach a given corner area, to carve out a finite-dimensional space of states for a causal diamond, from which it obtains the diamond's entropy. That step needs the clock to be a self-adjoint operator, but the clock is the exponential of a squared quantum field over an interval with sharp ends. This candidate tests it in the linearised radiative sector about a round cone, quantised in a stated natural Fock realisation compatible with the proposal's short-distance behaviour. Every Gaussian state gives probability one to configurations of infinite focusing, and without a regulator the Weyl-ordered focusing form is infinite on every state with second moments. In the Fock realisation the Weyl-ordered zero-point value grows like K² in the number K of radial modes; the normal-ordered ground value is of order −K and the normal-ordered form is not an operator on finite-particle vectors; and the Wick-ordered clock, positive and with the classical vacuum reading 1 − ε, is a quadratic form that is not closable, every closable form below it being zero. So the three natural prescriptions fail to provide the required clock with the specified domain and properties; this is not a claim that no clock can exist. For the cap cost used to count states the paper gives the exact Weyl law N(E) = (1 − ε³)E³/(1152π⁷) and the configuration-count constant, and shows that summed over tensor harmonics the normal-ordered cost is unbounded below and, at every sufficiently large fixed radial cutoff, not diagonalisable by an implementable Bogoliubov transformation; the continuum case is open. Limits: linearised sector and one natural realisation that the proposal does not force; the results do not show that the full non-linear construction fails. The mechanisms behind two results are Helfer's (1996, 1999). AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 51-page paper with a context-first introduction, written proofs of all theorems and propositions, a status table of what is and is not shown, open problems and an AI-use statement. Python scripts (numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, matplotlib 3.11.2): mode functions and kernels, the cap cost and its frequency solver, a truncated Fock space for the Wick-ordered clock, one check script per group of results, a script for the revision results and convergence diagnostics, and 16 automated tests, with recorded logs. Every check exits with status 1 on failure, also under python -O. The computations test constants and finite truncations; they do not certify the theorems. A clean release replay of every script in optimised mode reproduced every console log byte for byte and the JSON logs within a declared relative tolerance; shifting the expected Wick vacuum reading makes the tests fail. Linux CI reruns the fast suites with a negative control.

keyResults: Theorem A and Proposition 5.1 (proof, any representation): every Gaussian state gives probability one to shear configurations with infinite focusing on every subinterval; without a regulator the Weyl-ordered focusing form is +∞ on every state with second moments.
Theorem B (proof): with K radial modes the Weyl-ordered ground value on [a, b] is π² ln(b/a) K²/(2 s_p (1 − ε)²) (1 + O(K^(−1/4))), coefficient 14.03 on the whole generator at ε = 0.1.
Theorem C (proof): the normal-ordered ground value lies between −C₁K − C₂ ln K and −cK; the form is not an operator on finite-particle vectors.
Theorem D (proof, central result): the Wick-ordered clock form is positive with vacuum reading 1 − ε, is not closable, and every closable form below it is zero.

Theorems E–G (proof): cap-cost Weyl law N(E) = (1 − ε³)E³/(1152π⁷) + O(E^(5/2)) and log D coefficient 0.0648; the normal-ordered cost summed over harmonics is unbounded below and, at every sufficiently large fixed radial cutoff, not implementably diagonalisable; the continuum case is open.

Scope and credit: linearised sector in a stated natural Fock realisation compatible with the source; the three natural prescriptions fail, which is not a claim that no clock can exist; mechanisms behind Theorems C and G are Helfer's (1996, 1999).

decisionObject.description: Decide whether the gravitational clock and the cap cost of the null-cone quantisation of gravity can be self-adjoint operators under the natural orderings, and if not, which mechanisms obstruct them.
decisionObject.scope: Linearised radiative sector about a round past light cone, quantised in a natural Fock realisation compatible with the source; Weyl, normal and Wick ordering of the focusing integral and the clock; the cap cost summed over tensor harmonics.
